metadata.name: MPSN-Compatible Procedure Reference Database
metadata.description: A structured sample database compatible with MMA MPSN (Medical Procedures and Services Nomenclature) Version 2.0 (2020). Built for the Sabah Smart City medical bill checker hackathon MVP.
metadata.copyright_notice: The full MMA MPSN database is copyright of the Malaysian Medical Association (MMA). Reproduction requires written permission from MMA (secretary@mma.org.my). This file is a DEMO-ONLY compatible schema with sample entries — it does NOT reproduce copyrighted MPSN content. For production, a full MPSN licence must be obtained from MMA.
metadata.how_to_get_full_database: Contact MMA: 4th Floor, MMA House, 124 Jalan Pahang, Kuala Lumpur. Email: secretary@mma.org.my. Apply in writing for a licence to use MPSN data.
metadata.pitch_note: For judges: this database is intentionally structured to be MPSN-compatible. In production, this would be populated with the full licensed MPSN v2.0 dataset from MMA — our proposed partner. The schema and flagging logic are the same; only the data density changes.

mpsn_structure_overview.Part_A: Consultation fees and general medical procedures (outpatient, inpatient, specialty-specific)
mpsn_structure_overview.Part_B: Surgical procedures classified into 25 categories (Minor 1 through Complex Major 5), with a separate anaesthesiologist fee code per procedure
mpsn_structure_overview.lookup_tables: 5x5 Look-Up Tables map surgical procedure categories to fee amounts for both surgeon and anaesthesiologist
mpsn_structure_overview.source: MMA MPSN 5th Edition, Version 2.0 (2020), publicly described in MSA journal and Scribd overview documents

surgical_categories_part_b.description: The 25 surgical categories from MPSN Part B, from least to most complex. Each procedure in Part B is assigned one of these categories. The category determines the maximum fee from Schedule 13.
surgical_categories_part_b.note: Actual RM fee values per category are set in Schedule 13 of PHFSA 2006 (gazetted, public). Sample fee ranges below are indicative — verify against the gazetted document.

schedule_13_category_fee_reference.IMPORTANT: All fee values above are INDICATIVE ONLY. Must be replaced with exact values from the gazetted Schedule 13 document before production use.

fee_rule_from_phfsa.multiple_procedures_same_incision: The lesser procedure must not exceed 50% of the fee for the major procedure
fee_rule_from_phfsa.repeat_procedure: Second repeat <= 50% of first; third repeat <= 25% of first
fee_rule_from_phfsa.local_anaesthetic_by_operator: Additional charge not exceeding 20% of the procedure fee may be levied
fee_rule_from_phfsa.source: PHFSA Regulations 2006, Schedule 13, Regulation 433 — gazetted, public

procedures.name: Outpatient consultation — General Practitioner, initial visit
procedures.schedule_ref: Schedule 7 (GP clinics) / Schedule 13 Part A (GP in private hospital)
flag_rules: OVERCHARGE: billed > 125 (above legal cap)
UPCODE_CHECK: verify this is truly a GP, not a specialist — if a specialist consultation is billed at GP rates to understate charges, that is also a miscoding
procedures.notes: Most common line item on outpatient bills. The RM30-125 range reflects complexity; simple visits near RM30, complex near RM125.

procedures.name: Outpatient consultation — Specialist, initial visit
flag_rules: OVERCHARGE: billed > 235 (above legal cap)
DUPLICATE: same specialist consultation billed twice same date
UPCODE: GP visit billed as specialist visit
procedures.notes: If a patient sees multiple specialists in one admission, each may bill separately — each capped at RM235 initial.

procedures.name: Outpatient consultation — Specialist, follow-up visit
flag_rules: OVERCHARGE: billed > 150
UPCODE: follow-up billed as initial visit to charge higher rate — very common error
procedures.notes: VERIFY exact Schedule 13 follow-up cap before production use.

procedures.name: Ward visit — specialist, daily inpatient review
flag_rules: DUPLICATE: ward visit billed on same day as outpatient consultation (usually should not both appear)
OVERCHARGE: billed > 100 per daily ward visit
QUANTITY: more ward visit charges than inpatient days — impossible
procedures.notes: Verify exact cap. A common error: ward visit billed AND outpatient consultation billed on the same date.

procedures.name: Electrocardiogram (ECG / EKG)
flag_rules: BUNDLING: ECG is often considered part of a consultation — check if it should be bundled
DUPLICATE: ECG billed multiple times on same day without clinical justification
procedures.notes: Verify exact Schedule 13 cap. ECG interpretation and ECG recording are sometimes billed separately — watch for double billing.

procedures.name: Nebulisation treatment
flag_rules: QUANTITY: more than 3-4 nebulisations per day unusual — flag for review
DUPLICATE: billed separately when included in ward nursing care
procedures.notes: Common in paediatric and respiratory admissions.

procedures.name: Intravenous (IV) line insertion and maintenance
flag_rules: UNBUNDLING: IV insertion sometimes billed separately when it should be included in ward/procedure fee
QUANTITY: IV line re-siting charged multiple times — confirm it was genuinely re-sited
procedures.notes: IV fluid itself (e.g. Normal Saline, Dextrose) is a drug/consumable charge, separate from the IV insertion procedure.

procedures.name: Wound dressing / wound care
flag_rules: DUPLICATE: wound dressing billed daily PLUS included in nursing charge — possible double billing
QUANTITY: unusually high frequency — flag for review
procedures.notes: Dressing materials (gauze, bandage) may be billed separately as consumables.

procedures.name: Urinary catheterisation
flag_rules: DUPLICATE: catheter insertion AND catheter maintenance billed separately — check if one fee should be inclusive
procedures.notes: Catheter bag and tubing are consumables billed separately.

procedures.name: Wound suturing / laceration repair
procedures.schedule_ref: Schedule 13 Part A — minor surgical procedure
flag_rules: UPCODE: simple suture billed at complex laceration repair rate
UNBUNDLING: suture removal billed separately when it should be included in the original suture fee
procedures.notes: Fee depends on wound complexity and number of sutures.

procedures.name: Chest X-ray (PA view)
flag_rules: DUPLICATE: chest X-ray billed twice in same admission without justification
UNBUNDLING: X-ray 'taking' fee and radiologist 'reading' fee both billed — sometimes normal, sometimes double-billing
procedures.notes: Radiologist interpretation fee may legitimately appear as a separate line.

procedures.name: Ultrasound — abdomen
flag_rules: UPCODE: limited scan billed as complete abdominal ultrasound
DUPLICATE: same-region ultrasound repeated same day without documented clinical reason

procedures.name: CT scan — brain / head
flag_rules: UPCODE: plain CT billed at contrast-enhanced CT rate (higher)
DUPLICATE: CT of same region repeated within short period without justification
procedures.notes: Contrast agent (dye) may legitimately be charged separately as a drug/consumable.

procedures.name: Full Blood Count (FBC)
flag_rules: DUPLICATE: FBC billed multiple times same day without documented clinical need
UNBUNDLING: individual components of FBC (WBC, RBC, platelets) billed separately instead of as a panel
procedures.notes: Most common lab test ordered on admission.

procedures.name: Renal Function Test (RFT / U&E)
flag_rules: UNBUNDLING: creatinine, urea, electrolytes billed individually instead of as a panel

procedures.name: Liver Function Test (LFT)
flag_rules: UNBUNDLING: bilirubin, ALT, AST billed separately instead of as LFT panel

procedures.name: Random Blood Sugar (RBS / blood glucose)
flag_rules: QUANTITY: blood glucose checked many times per day for non-diabetic patient — flag for review

procedures.name: Urine Full Examination / UFEME
flag_rules: UNBUNDLING: dipstick test billed separately AND microscopy billed separately when UFEME covers both

procedures.name: Appendicectomy (open or laparoscopic)
flag_rules: ANAES_CHECK: anaesthesiologist fee must be cross-checked against the anaesthesiologist's fee look-up table for MAJ2 category
MULTIPLE_PROCEDURE: if another procedure done at same time, the lesser must be <= 50% of major
procedures.notes: Laparoscopic vs open may have different MPSN codes — flag if billing code does not match operation notes.

procedures.name: Caesarean section (C-section)
flag_rules: UPCODE: elective C-section billed at emergency/complex rate
UNBUNDLING: obstetrician fee, paediatric standby fee, and anaesthetic fee should all be separate — check for double-billing of any component
ANAES_CHECK: anaesthesia should be epidural or spinal — cross-check with anaesthesiologist fee
procedures.notes: Facility charges (OT, ward, consumables) are SEPARATE from this professional fee and are not regulated.

procedures.name: Coronary artery bypass graft (CABG)
flag_rules: MULTIPLE_PROCEDURE: if valve replacement done simultaneously, lesser procedure <= 50% of major
ANAES_CHECK: complex anaesthesia fee expected — verify against CMO3 look-up table
procedures.notes: Private total bill (including facility, ICU, devices) typically RM25,000-80,000. The Schedule 13 cap only covers the surgeon's professional fee.

procedures.name: Ward accommodation charge per day
procedures.schedule_ref: NOT regulated. Set by individual private hospitals. MPSN does not cover facility/hotel charges.
flag_rules: BENCHMARK: flag if significantly above the hospital's OWN published rate card
QUANTITY: ward days billed exceed actual admission duration — check against admission/discharge dates
DUPLICATE: ward charge AND room charge appearing as separate line items for same day
procedures.notes: Ward charges are NOT covered by MPSN or Schedule 13 — hospitals set their own rates. Government third-class ward is RM3/day (Fees Medical Order 2017). Flag on quantity mismatch, not price (since no legal cap exists).

procedures.name: Drug / Medication charges (generic reference)
procedures.schedule_ref: NOT regulated. Reference: Malaysia Medicine Price Guide (MyPriMe), MOH Pharmaceutical Services Programme. https://pharmacy.moh.gov.my/en/apps/drug-price
flag_rules: BENCHMARK: compare billed price per unit against MyPriMe suggested retail price
QUANTITY: quantity billed implausible for length of stay or condition (e.g. 30 tablets of antibiotic for a 2-day admission)
DUPLICATE: same drug appearing twice as different line items (e.g. branded and generic of same molecule)
procedures.notes: See reference_prices.json for specific verified drug entries (Paracetamol, Amoxicillin, Cetirizine, Diclofenac) sourced from MyPriMe Aug 2025.
